description: Contacted Hopkins through a newspaper advertisement; he provided a report on the history of beast attacks continuing from the early 19th century: victims were all drained of bodily fluids and had limbs torn off.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Hermes, sounds like the smuggling organization that got hit hard by the police recently."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "They're the ones who happened to save us."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Ah, so it was them? We got lucky."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player5 You and the cockroach in the corner stare at each other.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "They have a grudge against the newly risen Free Legion, yes, those neo-Nazi bastards who captured us."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It would be great if we could connect with them, but unfortunately, we don't have much to offer them."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David looks left and right, says a prayer in his heart for the deceased, and then focuses intently on examining the deceased's belongings.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: It seems there's nothing left in the room. Holding his nose, he pulls out a napkin, wraps it around the bathroom doorknob, and opens the door.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Having this card is enough; at least one person can infiltrate."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player5 There's nothing nauseating.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The mountains and soil listen to your wishes. Whatever the karma and retribution, fate now slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5 lifts the toilet lid, but unfortunately, there's nothing.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David follows Rabin to take a look; perhaps two people are better than one.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player3>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew puts away the bracelet and the Solomon's House pamphlet, thinking it would be good to know more about Lehman. Unfortunately, the man is dead, and trying to learn about him indirectly now is too awkward.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: It's not any better.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Seeing both of them busy in the bathroom, Andrew wonders if there's room for one more person and if he can help.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I didn't find anything. I can't hold it anymore; I need to go out and take a breath."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew takes over Driver Rabin's position and starts rummaging around in the bathroom.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player6>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Andrew slips and falls to the ground. As you try to push yourself up with your hands, you accidentally press down on the needle of a syringe.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What the hell is this? Ouch!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Unfortunately, this syringe seems to have some residual liquid inside, which just entered your vein through the needle.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew pulls out the needle and presses the puncture wound with his other hand to stop the bleeding.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "You okay, buddy?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: There's a small notebook next to the syringe.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It doesn't even hurt now; it actually feels good. My whole body doesn't hurt much."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David flips through the notebook.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The notebook is opened. The handwriting inside is unnervingly neat—unlike the scribbled notes of someone deep in drug addiction, it more closely resembles a precise log. Each page is divided into date, time, dosage, and brief remarks.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Go back where? I don't know." His mood dampens somewhat.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "April 26, 22:15—0.4g, intravenous, good effect."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "This Lehmann guy, it seems like he's experimenting on himself, testing the dosage on himself."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player3>'s Medicine check result:

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Go downstairs and find Gray. "Schiller seems to have been pricked by a needle, you go check on him. I'll watch the car."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gray believes Lehmann meticulously recorded and calculated his drug doses to ensure he got just enough "high" without endangering his life.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: This notebook seems like it will be very useful to Andrew later... Standing on the shoulders of giants.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "He tried to maintain the dosage at a level that gave him pleasure without risking his life. This guy is the rational type among addicts."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Dying from an overdose doesn't seem like Lehmann's style."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: All, roll Idea.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The mountains and soil hear your wishes. Whatever the karma and retribution, fate now slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player6

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and now you want to gamble on the one with no trace?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: When the spark of inspiration suddenly flashes, your world warps bizarrely.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The mountains and soil hear your wishes. Whatever the karma and retribution, fate now slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The euphoria is fleeting, replaced by an unbearable pain. The brain cannot process such vast information; it resists, struggles, screams. Your thoughts seem torn into countless parallel fragments of consciousness, forced to swallow these indigestible visual scenes. If you don't avert your gaze immediately, your sanity might completely collapse.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew crouches on the floor, eyes tightly shut, holding his head in pain.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player6>'s Sanity check:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison is hit by waves of dry heaving, clutching her stomach trying to ease the discomfort.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: And player5, watching the car downstairs.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David feels a bit dizzy and nauseous. Was it something he ate this morning?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You notice a person in uniform approaching the main entrance of the apartment building.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Slip another ten marks to the apartment manager, signal him to handle it, and immediately run upstairs to call everyone down.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Roll Education.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Cops are here, time to scram!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then you guys quickly put everything back in order and sneak away like thieves.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Education check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The others, in their透视状态, see the manager making exaggerated gestures, seemingly trying to talk the bailiff into leaving, and nervously glancing towards the apartment. The bailiff looks somewhat troubled and prepares to leave.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Then follow the retreat.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Alarm bells ring in player5's mind; in his panic, he believes this person is definitely here to arrest everyone.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You guys immediately, instantly, quickly leave. If there's a back door, great; if not, dash upstairs, avoid the bailiff, and come down later.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Although not fully aware of what was happening, Andrew simply followed whatever others were doing.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: This rundown apartment has only one way in and out, with no other exits.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison calms herself down and discreetly heads downstairs normally while gesturing to her colleagues to split up.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We're too conspicuous, aren't we?" Andrew muttered quietly, but still followed everyone's arrangement.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David then confirms everything is fine and discreetly heads downstairs.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As you cautiously make your way downstairs, the uniformed man is already long gone. The superintendent still looks at you suspiciously, "Why are you so scared of a bailiff?... Just give me back the keys and leave quickly. I've never seen you before, and don't drag me into your business." He seems convinced of something, feeling that you're up to no good.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What happened? Oh, a bailiff."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "None of your business, please leave. Only those aboveboard are welcome here."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If it's just one person, it doesn't seem like they're here to chase us, but it's always good to be careful." Back in the car, Alison reassures her colleagues.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew looks utterly confused, walks out of the apartment, and returns to the car.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Get in the car, get in the car.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Get in the car, next stop.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The story record of the Algorithm of the Heart has resumed, currently with 3741 text recorded. Continue! There will definitely be gains today!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Time rewinds.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Education check result: D100=96/85. The result is succe... oh no, it's a failure. Perhaps there's still a way to remedy it. <player6>'s Education check result: D100=89/45. The result is succe... oh no, it's a failure. Perhaps there's still a way to remedy it.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: What is a bailiff?

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player3>'s Education check result: D100=73/85 Success. A close success. Adventurer, boldness always has its rewards.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You only notice that this person's uniform is quite different from the police uniforms you saw earlier at the police station.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "SWAT!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Folks, probably not a proper cop coming to nab us. Look, he's not fully armed either."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Armed police! — Why is there only one?" "You're right, what's he here for?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David assesses. "If he comes up, we'll gang up and take him out. We're already wanted anyway." "Probably just passing by."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew picks up the syringe and gets ready.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's best not to resort to violence if possible. He might not recognize us as wanted criminals." Alison thinks it's better not to alert the enemy.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Hope he doesn't come up and just leaves."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Actually, we're just a bunch of, uh, drug addicts looking for medicine."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Your clairvoyant state ends after seeing the superintendent go up to talk to the uniformed man, and then a panting player5 bursts in.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew crouches on the ground, holding his head, looking extremely distressed.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "What's going on?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Wait, what just happened?" Alison feels something is off.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "I need to catch my breath first..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "What's wrong with you all? You don't look so good?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Did we all just see a policeman downstairs?" Alison held her forehead, "player5, what's going on?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yes, yes."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We... don't know what we experienced... It was like seeing the situation downstairs from a strange perspective. Is there a policeman down there?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Nodded, "There is a hat coming this way. I was afraid he'd notice us, so I came up first."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Is it a hallucination caused by some drug here... No, that's not right either. All three of us saw the same thing, and there really is a policeman coming. This is too weird." Alison broke out in a cold sweat.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "But, we weren't doing anything special? How did we suddenly get X-ray vision? Is it related to this room?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Uh, ah!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Now's not the time to talk about this. What should we do now?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Secretly search the room for *goods*, which can be used as a disguise later, and might have other uses.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I don't want to attract the hat's attention so quickly."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "If he comes up, we take him out. He doesn't look like he's coming up."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player6 Andrew found half a bag of "white powder".

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We can also take the opportunity to gather some information, use our interrogation skills."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Put it in the pocket. This isn't for injecting. Look for some tinfoil.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison noticed Andrew's actions, "From a doctor and colleague's perspective, I advise you not to touch that stuff."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What if it's useful later? We need all the help we can get right now."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David thought about it and felt they should learn about the police's case results. He straightened his collar to hide his gun and went downstairs to find the caretaker and that bailiff, hoping he hadn't been sent away yet.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "If he calls for backup, it's over."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Attacking a policeman proactively if we haven't been discovered is too reckless. Let's try to make contact. If anything seems off, then we act." Alison stopped the excited Andrew.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "...Alright, be careful."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison followed David downstairs.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew started looking for tinfoil and an alcohol lamp.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Leave the room and find a spot at the stairwell where you can see the situation of the two from a distance, keeping watch on the surroundings.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After experiencing the ultimate pleasure, Andrew was a bit impatient.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Andrew, if you don't want to be the next Lehman, I suggest you stay away from that stuff."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Of course, of course, I'm being careful."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David listens to what's being said, offers a cigarette to both the caretaker and the bailiff, and lights one for himself.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The uniformed man first eyed you suspiciously from head to toe, then carefully took the cigarette and tapped it, "Let's get this straight, I can't help you get anyone out or anything."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison breathed a sigh of relief.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After confirming there was nothing in the cigarette, he borrowed your lighter, lit it, and took a puff. "Whoa, British cigarettes, nice stuff."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "You have a good eye. They were quite a hassle to buy. Why would I make things difficult for you? I just wanted to offer you a smoke and ask a few little questions, just casual talk." David eagerly lit the uniformed man's cigarette. "Absolutely won't trouble you at all." Since he mentioned helping to get someone out, can David deduce from this that this guy is a police officer related to the prison system? Or check the guy's shoulder insignia; MI6 should have learned about such things.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The administrator was somewhat confused. He was just told to send others away, and now someone is being called down from upstairs to chat. However, this clever person wisely didn't interrupt. "What's the matter? Do you have friends going to court soon?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David checks if this guy is armed? If not, he can relax and ask questions. "Not exactly, it's probably a concluded matter. I knew someone who used to live here. I wanted to ask you about this Mr. Lehmann, since he owed me some money." Would the police inventory the deceased's belongings or financial situation? Perhaps David can use this to start the conversation.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Lehmann? You'd better give up on that early. His belongings were auctioned, and the proceeds first go to repay the bank. The administrator already told you about his situation, right? Ran away from debt. You'd best consider that money gone." "I came here to inform him that the property forcibly seized by the federal court on June 29th, due to failure to redeem it in time, will be auctioned at the Federal Judicial Auction House on the 5th at 14:00. The proceeds will be used to repay his debts to the bank." "That's just how it is in this line of work, damn it, we've become deliverymen, completely lacking police authority." After saying this, he complained indifferently.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "God, how could this guy owe money everywhere? No sense of contract at all, he really should go to hell." David muttered on purpose. "How much did he owe?" "Ah, it's all about making a living, not easy." David understood implicitly, deeply empathizing with the bailiff, and lit another cigarette for him.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Who knows? Probably ten or twenty thousand Marks."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "What did the court seize from him? Will the auction proceeds be enough to cover the debt? Or are we just going to be the suckers?" David deliberately expressed doubt.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Don't know. I'm just the messenger. Most likely not enough. I've seen plenty of people like this. If their family had anything valuable, they would have pawned it long ago for drugs. If you're interested, you could try to snag something at the auction; judicial auctions start at low prices."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Hey, guess I'll have to try my luck. Getting some of my money back would be good." David sighed. "Thanks for telling me this news, otherwise others would snatch it all and I'd be at a total loss." He handed the remaining half-pack of cigarettes to the bailiff. "Thanks, buddy."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "See you." He unceremoniously pocketed the cigarettes and left the apartment.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Gestures to Alison to go back and continue searching the place.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Not looking for us," tells Schiller and player5.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Roll Idea.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and will you now gamble on the untraceable one? <player4>'s Idea check result: D100=59/85 Success. Move forward quickly, be decisive. No danger ahead. <player5>'s Idea check result: D100=42/85 Hard Success. To achieve this under such circumstances, you truly are my companion. <player3>'s Idea check result: D100=58/80 Success. A close success. Adventurer, boldness always has its reward.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gray remembers not seeing a court auction notice on the apartment door; it must have been removed.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "So that's what was stuck on the door before."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What, what thing?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "The judicial auction notice."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Probably torn off by someone. Who would do that, and for what purpose?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Oh, I see. Wonder what he has left. It's such a mess, no one cleaned it up." "We're done here. Should we go visit that radio association?" "I have a feeling they're mixed up with all these strange things, especially that beast attack. Maybe that's the key to the problem."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Haddin is involved in so many complicated matters... This is already several lives lost. I hope we can find him smoothly later." Alison sighed.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "He absolutely must be alive."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We're still one step removed from Haddin." "We lack direct evidence pointing to Haddin's whereabouts."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "After all, he's been missing for so many days now."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The banned substance, could it possibly point to drugs?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "So, where do we go next?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Later, let's ask the administrator about Lehmann's character. Then go to Solomon or Hermes, or the radio association."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Hermes seems a bit dangerous, no safer than that factory. At least Solomon's House and the radio association seem more friendly."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I think it might be a bit early for Hermes, there's too little information. But this suggests Lehmann probably has some smuggled goods too."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Either way, we'll have to go there sooner or later."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Let's head downstairs first."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Turning to the caretaker with a smile, "How was Lehmann usually around here? Has he made any enemies recently?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I really can't stand this place for another second."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "This guy used to have a decent job, but gambling and drug addiction led to personal bankruptcy, leaving him with huge debts to the bank. He had no choice but to join a smuggling and intelligence gang, often getting beaten for stealing, so he's always seen with bruises. However, he's not stupid, quite methodical, always manages to get money and pay the rent."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "You're very well-informed, sir."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Has he been acting unusual lately? Please think carefully." Find David to give him a cigarette.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Don't know, I don't have any particular habits. As long as the rent is paid on time, I can't be bothered to observe what others are like."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright, thank you for your trouble."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew walks towards the door calmly.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go." Before leaving, try to restore the seal to its original state.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Depart.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: So you leave this place with an excessive concentration of scum.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Not sure if the average concentration will rise or fall after we leave.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The association is located in a three-story old office building in the suburbs. From outside, tall antennas can be seen protruding from the roof, some still emitting a buzzing sound.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: This chatterbox has really provided us with a lot of help.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: The radio association does this too? Andrew is somewhat puzzled.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Should someone stay to watch the car?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Probably no one would steal a car here. The situation outside doesn't seem as tense as we imagined."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Better safe than sorry. In case anything happens, it's good to have someone for support."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Then the rest can swagger right in.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then follow them in. Boost our courage.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hello, we heard you're looking for volunteer investigators? We're very interested in mysterious beasts and such." Find the front desk and approach to strike up a conversation.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You enter the first floor, which is an open hall divided into several areas by several long tables. Various radio equipment, oscilloscopes, disassembled transistor radios, and hand-drawn circuit diagrams are scattered messily on the long tables. Red, green, and yellow indicator lights flicker in the semi-dark space. Several men are sitting around a table, talking in low voices, occasionally adjusting equipment or hastily writing parameters in a notebook. One of them is poking at an old shortwave transceiver with a screwdriver, emitting intermittent "beep—beep—" signal sounds from time to time.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Well, we're quite interested for now."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Let me introduce myself. I'm Erich Winter, president of the South German Civil Radio Association."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Charles Turing

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Charles Turing. Enthusiast of folklore and urban legends, radio enthusiast." Shake his hand.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Hopkins, pleased to meet you."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hello, hello, I'm glad our advertisement in the newspaper proved useful."
